slot.brief: Investigate continuity and differentiability of a piecewise function at a point; find parameter(s) and check derivative existence via one-sided limits.

stem: For $a>0$, define $$f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{e^{ax}-1-ax}{x^2},&x<0,\\2+cx,&x\ge0.\end{cases}$$ If $f$ is differentiable at $0$, find $(a,c)$.

verdicts.working: Using the Taylor expansion, the left-hand limit is \(a^2/2\), so continuity requires \(a^2/2=2\). Since \(a>0\), \(a=2\). The left derivative is \(a^3/6\); matching it to the right derivative \(c\) gives \(c=4/3\).

working:
For $x<0$, $\dfrac{e^{ax}-1-ax}{x^2}=\dfrac{a^2}{2}+\dfrac{a^3}{6}x+O(x^2)$. Continuity gives $a^2/2=2$, so $a=2$. The left derivative is $a^3/6$; matching it with the right derivative $c$ gives $c=4/3$.

Independent check: Using the Taylor expansion, the left-hand limit is \(a^2/2\), so continuity requires \(a^2/2=2\). Since \(a>0\), \(a=2\). The left derivative is \(a^3/6\); matching it to the right derivative \(c\) gives \(c=4/3\).
solution:
Using $e^{ax}=1+ax+\dfrac{a^2x^2}{2}+\dfrac{a^3x^3}{6}+O(x^4)$,
$$f(x)=\dfrac{a^2}{2}+\dfrac{a^3}{6}x+O(x^2)\quad(x<0).$$
Continuity at $0$ gives $a^2/2=2$, hence $a=2$ since $a>0$. Matching the left derivative $a^3/6$ with the right derivative $c$ gives $c=4/3$.
